solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailor by old platform covers wreck

indicators.note: the platform wraps itself round the sailor and the old

parts.note: a stage is a raised platform; it goes round AB + O

explanation.surface: A sailor on an old platform looks on at a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: "Wreck" looks like a noun to go with the sailor, but it is the verb: to sabotage something is to wreck it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sabotage a plan or machine is to wreck it deliberately.

clue.text: One abandoning capital for surfing destination?

definitions.note: the place where a couch surfer ends up sleeping; plural-free noun like the answer

indicators.note: the one is left behind, so it drops out of the city's name

parts.note: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone quits a capital city to head for the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfing' is couch surfing, not riding waves; SOFIA with I 'abandoning' it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch surfer stays overnight on a friend's couch, so the settee is where the surfing ends up.

clue.text: Mature bird demolished fish in main area

definitions.note: the main is the sea, and this is a notorious stretch of ocean

indicators.note: a building demolished is knocked down and its parts lie jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grown bird was wrecked while fishing out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges MATUREBIRD into BERMUDATRI; 'main' is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is a region of the western Atlantic, famous for ships and planes said to vanish there.

clue.text: Child completely stone cold finally came to

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of stone and cold

explanation.surface: A child knocked out stone cold finally regains consciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: "Came to" pretends to mean woke up after being knocked out; here it is what a bill does when it came to fifty pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that came to a sum totalled that sum.

clue.text: Labour good for Charlie in shipping?

indicators.note: good is put in place of Charlie, the usual sense of one thing standing for another

parts.note: craft, a vessel in shipping, means boats or vessels collectively, i.e. shipping
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Asks whether hard work in the shipping trade swaps one sailor's name for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the C of CRAFT for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is informal British for hard work or toil, matching labour as a noun.

clue.text: Rod starts to import US Motown and soft metal

indicators.note: take the starting letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Rod starts importing American Motown records and soft metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Rod Stewart and music genres; "soft metal" is quite literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Barium is a soft, silvery alkaline-earth metal.

clue.text: Trap contingent of westbound French submarines

indicators.note: a contingent is a part of a larger group, so the answer is a part of the words
in the across direction west is leftward, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: the letters run from the end of frencH into SUBMArines

explanation.surface: A group of French submarines heads west to set a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: "Westbound" is an across-clue reversal word used in a down clue; it still just means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as a verb, to lie in wait and spring on someone is to trap them.

clue.text: Popular pieces in parade followed by high profile player

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the parade
A-LIST comes after the rest

parts.note: to parade is to strut; it goes round MEN
the A-list are the most famous people

explanation.surface: A popular item in a parade is followed by a famous player.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces are chessmen, a common crossword source of MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist plays a musical instrument, so is a player.

clue.text: Reported behaviour on hot river residence

parts.note: manner = behaviour; said aloud it matches MANOR
H = hot, as on a tap
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A report on someone's behaviour on a hot river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a crossword favourite among English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor house is the main residence of a country estate.

clue.text: Sticking Bill in this location with conservationists

parts.note: NT = National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a bill up here with the approval of conservationists.
explanation.walkthrough: "With" simply joins NT on the end. Adherent is used here as the adjective meaning sticking fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherent as an adjective means sticking, adhering.

clue.text: Direct Henry feeding bear behind tree

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it; H goes inside
H = henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An instruction to put Henry feeding a bear behind a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bear" is the verb, as in "I can't stand it".
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for experience gained yourself, with no go-between: a direct account is one from the source.

clue.text: Not one close family member recalled plain beasts

indicators.note: called back, so read backwards

parts.note: no = not one, as in 'no sheep'

explanation.surface: Not one close relative remembered the ordinary animals.
explanation.walkthrough: "Plain" looks like "ordinary" but means the Great Plains, where bison roam.
explanation.definitionFit: Bison are the beasts of the North American plains.

clue.text: Con stealer of chips that are not digitally secured?

definitions.meaning: con as a verb: to fool or swindle someone

definitions.text: stealer of chips that are not digitally secured?
definitions.meaning: seagulls snatch chips from people not holding them tightly

explanation.surface: A con artist steals poker chips that are not locked by digital security.
explanation.walkthrough: "Digitally" means with the fingers, not electronically, and the chips are fried ones at the British seaside, where gulls grab them.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull is to dupe, and the seaside gull steals chips from loose hands.

clue.text: Three had regularly selected more reliable fund manager

indicators.note: letters picked at a regular interval, every other one

explanation.surface: Three people chose a more reliable fund manager.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters run across the two words as if they were one: ThReE hAd.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages the funds of a club or society.

clue.text: Quiet about Hearts supporter that's raised goal record?

indicators.note: about in its sense of around
in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a core is a heart, as of an apple
a golf tee supports the ball; it is raised, so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: A Hearts football fan has quietly raised a record of the goals.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club, which makes the surface about football; in the wordplay it is just CORES.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoresheet records the goals, hence the question mark on a slightly loose definition.

clue.text: Spanish man turned on male English shepherds

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed after the rest

parts.note: señor is Spanish for a man, Mr; turned, it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A Spanish man turns against the English male shepherds.
explanation.walkthrough: "Shepherds" is a verb here: to guide or look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaperone someone is to shepherd them, keeping an eye on them.

clue.text: Port boys periodically manage device used in canal

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter

parts.note: the even letters of pOrT bOyS

explanation.surface: Boys in a port occasionally handle a gadget used on a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the ear canal, not a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the instrument a doctor uses to look into the ear canal.

clue.text: Skinned meat items maybe loaded into barrel

indicators.note: skinning strips the outside, so the outer letters of the meat are removed

parts.note: gammon is cured ham, a meat

explanation.surface: A butcher's skinned cuts being packed into a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinned' strips G and N off GAMMON. The barrel is a gun's, not a cask, which kills the meat-packing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition such as cartridges is what gets loaded into the barrel of a gun.

clue.text: Vicar cutting cold fool last of the crack

indicators.note: take the final letter of 'the'

explanation.surface: A vicar interrupts a cold fool at the last of the joke.
explanation.walkthrough: "Crack" looks like a joke to go with the fool, but it is a fissure. Rev. is short for Reverend, the title of a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack, especially in a glacier.

clue.text: Two military units seldom seen

explanation.surface: Two army units are hardly ever spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery and Royal Engineers are British Army corps, standard crossword abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rare bird is one that is seldom seen.

clue.text: Tracks profit on renovated street in recession

indicators.note: made over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ST = street, in recession so it goes backwards

explanation.surface: An economic piece: profit tracked on a renovated street during a recession.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is financial news; "Tracks" is the plural noun, the marks left by feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracks as a plural noun: the marks left in mud or snow, which a tracker follows.

clue.text: Minister beat ten defenceless guards

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A government minister has beaten ten helpless security guards.
explanation.walkthrough: "Minister" is the verb, to minister to someone, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean looking after someone's needs, as a nurse does for a patient.

clue.text: Epic fight with cross characters holding clubs

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it within your grasp

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T, shaped like a cross
C = clubs, the card suit; it goes inside TAUS

explanation.surface: An epic fight between people who are cross.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cross characters" sounds like angry people but means letters shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus is the 1960 Kubrick epic film about the gladiator revolt.

clue.text: Jack briefly working for place that may fix locks

parts.note: a jack (tar) is a sailor, a SALT; it loses its T

explanation.surface: Jack briefly works for a locksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: The locks are locks of hair, not door locks, so the place is a hair salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair salon fixes locks of hair.

clue.text: Container lorry's first on road heading for Rome?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Appian Way leading to Rome

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of lorry's

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: A freight lorry setting off along the road towards Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman roads were named Via (Via Appia); 'lorry's first' is L, put 'on' (after) it in this across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle for holding liquids, so a type of container.

clue.text: Visit capsized vessels avoiding half of loch

indicators.note: in a down clue a capsized thing is upside down, so the letters run backwards
the vessels steer clear of those letters, so they are dropped

parts.note: the second half of the word loch is CH

explanation.surface: Boats overturned while keeping away from part of a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops CH from YACHTS to leave YATS, and 'capsized' turns that over. A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a period spent somewhere as a guest, a sense close to a visit.

clue.text: Joy almost goes after exposed lean bird

indicators.note: to go after is to follow, so the shortened joy comes after the stripped lean

parts.note: GLEE, joy, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Joy almost vanishes after exposing a thin bird.
explanation.walkthrough: "Lean" is the word to be stripped, not the bird's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the eagle is one bird among many.

clue.text: Top car son struck with king aboard

indicators.note: a passenger aboard is inside the vehicle

parts.note: the Volkswagen Polo is a car
R = rex, king; it goes inside HIT

explanation.surface: A top car has hit a son with the king on board.
explanation.walkthrough: "Top" looks like an adjective, best, but it is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the collared short-sleeved shirt is one kind of top, the garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Walks from hotel leaving clothing

indicators.note: hotel departs from the clothing, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone strolls out of a hotel, leaving their clothes behind.
explanation.walkthrough: THREADS is slang for clothes; 'leaving' takes out the H for hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to step or walk, so treads matches walks as a verb.

clue.text: Experts carrying pole attempt descent

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within

parts.note: N = north pole; it goes inside ACES

explanation.surface: Experts carrying a pole attempt to climb down.
explanation.walkthrough: "Descent" looks like climbing down but means lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Your descent is your ancestry, the line you come from.
